content.raw:
Advocate for Criminal Matters in Pimple Saudagar

Pimple Saudagar, Pimple Gurav and Rahatni are residential areas of Pimpri-Chinchwad. Most of Pimple Saudagar and all of Pimple Gurav fall within Sangvi Police Station of the Pimpri-Chinchwad Police Commissionerate; there is no separate Pimple Gurav police station. Matters from these areas that commonly reach an advocate are matrimonial cases under Section 85 BNS (old 498A IPC) and the Domestic Violence Act, cheque bounce complaints under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, property-related FIRs and cyber fraud complaints.

Advocate Akash R. Chikate has an office at Pimple Gurav, about 2–4 km from Pimple Saudagar, open by appointment, and a main office at Shivajinagar near the Pune District and Sessions Court. He appears before the Pimpri court, the Pune District and Sessions Court and the Bombay High Court.

Legal Services Available

  • Anticipatory Bail — before police arrest you in a domestic or financial dispute
  • Bail After Arrest — remand representation and bail applications at the Pimpri court and the Pune District and Sessions Court
  • 498A / DV Act Defence — for accused and family members
  • Cheque Bounce (NI Act) — both filing and defending S.138 matters
  • Cybercrime — online fraud FIRs registered at Sangvi Police Station or the Pimpri-Chinchwad Cyber Police Station
  • FIR Quashing — Bombay High Court intervention for false or frivolous complaints

Call or WhatsApp for an immediate consultation. First consultation is free and confidential.

Arrested or Called by Sangvi Police: The First 24 Hours

  1. Ask why. The police must tell the arrested person the grounds of arrest (Section 47 BNSS) and inform a relative or friend (Section 48 BNSS). Ask for the FIR number and the sections applied.
  2. A notice is not an arrest. A notice under Section 35 BNSS (old 41A CrPC) asks you to appear and cooperate. Keep a copy and take advice before you reply or attend.
  3. Production before a Magistrate. An arrested person must be produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours (Section 58 BNSS). Sangvi Police Station cases go to a Magistrate court of the Pimpri-Chinchwad court, which currently sits at Nehrunagar, Pimpri.
  4. Bail. In bailable offences, bail can be given at the police station. In non-bailable offences, the application goes to the Magistrate (Section 480 BNSS) or the Sessions Court (Section 483 BNSS). Where an arrest is only feared, anticipatory bail is sought under Section 482 BNSS.
  5. In matrimonial cases, relatives named in the FIR who live elsewhere can apply for anticipatory bail without waiting for the police to contact them.
  6. What to collect. FIR copy or number, the arrest memo, any notice received, identity and address proof of the accused and of a surety, and a short note of dates.

This is general information, not advice on your matter.

Further Questions from Pimple Saudagar

Is there an advocate's office in Pimple Saudagar or Pimple Gurav?

Yes. The practice has an office at Ravikaran Heights, Shivdatta Nagar, Pimple Gurav, about 2–4 km from Pimple Saudagar. It is open by appointment.

A cheque I issued has bounced and I received a legal notice. What is the time limit?

Under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, the drawer has 15 days from receiving the notice to pay the cheque amount. If it is not paid, the complainant can file a complaint within one month after that period ends. Reply to the notice in writing and keep proof of delivery.
